main_body: Tall brick townhouse: slate mansard roof with a dormer and chimney, an orange cornice, and three storeys of brick wall with windows, a balcony and a green door
top_band: Blue-grey slate roof, rows ~10-42: a flat roof panel at rows ~10-24, then the lighter-to-darker mansard slope below it. The orange cornice at rows ~43-46 forms the front edge.
evidence: Reading down the middle column: slate roof surface (flat top plus sloped mansard, ~28 rows), then the orange cornice line at rows ~43-46, then a dark grey stone band under it. Below that is the brick front face (~96 rows). The windows have stone surrounds, sills and dark inner frames, so they read as inset. The roof is a large readable surface, not a thin rim. The upper flat panel is somewhat elevation-like, but the sloped slate roof and the cornice overhang carry the 3/4 reading.

style.evidence: The brick has individual bricks in several tones and the slate has per-tile variation. The windows carry glass reflections and lit-interior gradients, and the stone trim is shaded in several steps. The outlines are a dark navy or brown lean tied to the neighbouring material rather than pure black. Per-tile colour counts look at least equal to the reference. No large flat fills. It would sit comfortably next to the Beodeul houses.
